title: Maximum Beauty of an Array After Applying Operation
statement:
You are given an integer array `nums` and a non-negative integer `k`. Each index `i` may be changed at most once: when you change it, `nums[i]` becomes any integer you like between `nums[i] - k` and `nums[i] + k` inclusive. You may change any set of indices, including none or all of them.

The *beauty* of an array is the length of its longest subsequence whose elements are all equal, that is, the largest count of positions holding one same value. Return the greatest beauty `nums` can have after your changes.
notes:
## Intuition

Each element can become any value in its own interval `[nums[i] - k, nums[i] + k]`. A group of elements can all be made equal exactly when their intervals share a common point, and since every interval has the same width `2k`, that happens when the group's largest and smallest values differ by at most `2 * k`. The order of `nums` does not matter for the answer, so sort it: the best group is then a contiguous window whose two ends differ by at most `2 * k`. A brute force would test every candidate common value and count reachable elements; the sorted window does it in one pass.

## Approach

1. Sort `nums` ascending.
2. Move `right` across the array, treating `nums[left..right]` as the window.
3. While `nums[right] - nums[left] > 2 * k`, the window cannot meet, so advance `left`.
4. The window is now valid; update `best` with its length `right - left + 1`.
5. Return `best`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [4,6,1,2]`, `k = 2`, so the allowed spread is 4. Sorted: `[1,2,4,6]`. `right = 0, 1, 2` keep `left = 0` (spreads 0, 1, 3), giving `best = 3`. At `right = 3` the spread `6 - 1 = 5` is too big, so `left` moves to 1 (`6 - 2 = 4`), window length 3. The answer is `3`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n log n) for sorting; the window scan is O(n) because `left` only moves forward.
- Space: O(1) beyond the sort.

## Pitfalls

- The allowed spread is `2 * k`, not `k`: both ends move toward each other.
- The comparison is strict: a spread of exactly `2 * k` is still fine.
- Beauty counts a subsequence, so the chosen elements need not be adjacent in the original array; that is why sorting is allowed.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `left`, `right` | ends of the current window in the sorted array |
| `best` | largest valid window length found so far |

narration.2: Sort so that any group that can be made equal forms a contiguous window.
narration.3: No window has been measured yet.
narration.4: The window starts at the first element.
narration.5: Extend the window to include nums[right].
narration.6: Is the spread too large for both ends to reach a common value?
narration.7: Yes: drop the smallest element from the window.
narration.9: The window now fits; remember its length if it is the largest.
narration.11: Return the size of the largest group that can be made equal.
